title: Speaker Recognition & Verification
service: SpeakerID: cosine scoring and EER over trial lists, a SQLite speaker registry, S-norm verification, online and agglomerative diarization

parts.lesson_anchor: Build It, Steps 2-3: cosine + threshold, EER from similarity pairs; Pitfalls: cosine on non-normalized embeddings
planted_bugs: eer is the lesson's Step 3 version: best starts at (1.0, 1.0, 0.0), whose gap is 0, so it never updates and always returns (1.0, 0.0)

parse_trials reads the VoxCeleb label with bool(label), and bool('0') is True; every trial becomes a target and eer raises ZeroDivisionError on the empty non-target list, one call away from the parser
cosine is the lesson code's raw dot product, which assumes unit vectors; on unnormalized embeddings the trial-list EER is 0.5 at threshold 25 instead of 0.25 at 0.8
eer recounts every score for every candidate threshold, O(T (S + D))
parts.timing_assert: eer on 6000 + 6000 scores under 0.1 s (the recount takes 1.1-1.8 s on Python 3.10-3.14; a sorted sweep 2-5 ms)
parts.overfix_guard: scores tied across classes cross the threshold together (an ungrouped sorted sweep gives 0.25 at 0.6, a merge that moves one class's ties at a time 0.625 at 0.6, instead of 0.375 at 0.7); all-equal scores give EER 0.5 at that score (a corner-initialized search returns threshold 0.0); a silent clip's zero embedding scores 0.0 (dividing by the norms raises ZeroDivisionError)

deviations: Part 1: the suggested FAR/FRR swap is replaced by the VoxCeleb trial-list label parsed with bool(label). Swapping the FA and FR names leaves this EER unchanged, while the parser bug gives the failure one call away from its root cause (ZeroDivisionError inside eer). FAR/FRR confusion is a Part 3 trap instead (FAR measured on target scores).
Part 1: the zero vector is a guard on the cosine fix, not a planted bug in l2_normalize. The lesson's l2_normalize already maps the zero vector to zeros, and its Step 2 cosine returns 0.0 for it.
Part 1: tie handling is the guard on the speed-up (a sorted sweep moves tied scores together), and the all-equal-scores case guards the corner-initialized fix of the starting gap.

Part 2: exact (sum, count) is tested as 'removing an enrollment restores the template bit-for-bit'. A float (sum, count) cache cannot meet it, so the reference recomputes from the stored raw embeddings with math.fsum. No enrollment-order check: Python 3.12's sum() is compensated, so plain sum() would pass on 3.12 and fail on 3.10/3.11.
Part 3: AS-norm (top_k per side) is tested next to S-norm. Threshold selection at a target FAR is the pure function threshold_at_far; calibrate and verify connect it to the S-norm scores.
Part 4: the wire format is RTTM, the diarization standard, instead of NDJSON, which 06/03 already uses.
